title: Failure modes + guardrails checklist — Auto-rollback on SLO breach
content:
Context
- We’re wiring rollout controller → SLO monitors → auto action (pause or rollback) on breach.
- This doc is a working checklist of “ways this goes wrong” + concrete guardrails to ship MVP safely.
- Focus is operational safety (avoid flapping + avoid making an incident worse), not perfect detection.

Definitions (for this doc)
- “Monitor” = a rollout-scoped SLO monitor (latency p95/p99, error-rate, saturation where relevant) with burn-rate semantics (fast/slow windows).
- “Auto action” = pause rollout OR rollback to last known-good (LKG) step/model version OR revert traffic split to baseline.
- “Scope” = service/route + model version + region + customer tier (and sometimes dedicated cluster id).

Assumptions / constraints
- Metrics and SLO toolkit queries are not instantaneous; staleness + lag are normal.
- Traffic during canaries can be low volume, especially for: small routes, single regions, customer-tier partitions.
- Tail latency moves for non-regression reasons (batching config changes, cache warmup/cold start, GPU saturation, upstream traffic shifts).
- We must avoid oscillation (roll back / re-advance / roll back) and avoid rollback storms across many concurrent rollouts.
- When telemetry is partially down, “doing nothing” may be safer than taking automated actions based on bad data.

Primary design goal (safety principle)
- Default posture: conservative, explainable, and bounded.
- Prefer “pause” when confidence is low; require stronger evidence for “rollback”.
- Always record: what we saw, why we acted/suppressed, and what guardrail fired (for audit + incident response).

Failure modes checklist + proposed guardrails

1) Metric lag / delayed ingestion
Symptoms
- SLO toolkit returns data that is 2–10 minutes behind real time.
- Fast-burn window shows breach but slow window hasn’t populated yet.
- Rollout step transitions happen faster than metrics can stabilize.

Risks
- False positive rollback (roll back due to old spike that already recovered).
- False negative (breach happened, but we missed it because data arrived late).

Guardrails
- Staleness detection: require monitor “as_of” timestamp within max_staleness_seconds.
  - Proposed default: 120s for Hosted, 180s for Dedicated, 300s for Private/on-prem (varies).
  - If stale: do NOT rollback; either (a) pause evaluation and emit “monitor_stale” event, or (b) pause rollout if policy says “fail-safe pause”.
- Step holdoff: after a rollout step change (traffic shift), wait N minutes before evaluating for rollback.
  - Proposed: 3 minutes minimum or “2x scrape_interval + 1x pipeline_lag estimate”.
- “Fast + slow window confirmation” requirement for rollback (see ADR-0127).
  - Rollback only when BOTH windows indicate burn rate > threshold (after holdoff).
  - Pause can trigger on fast window alone (policy-controlled).

2) Partial telemetry outage (missing series, missing labels, intermittent)
Symptoms
- Query returns empty timeseries for a subset of labels (e.g., missing per-model-version dimension).
- Only some regions report.
- Error budget calculators return “unknown” state.

Risks
- Interpreting “no data” as “good” (false negative).
- Interpreting “no data” as “bad” (false positive) causing unnecessary rollback.
- Rollout controller blocks / slows down due to retries.

Guardrails
- Explicit monitor state machine: OK | BREACH | NO_DATA | STALE | ERROR.
- Default: treat NO_DATA/ERROR as “cannot decide”, not as breach.
  - Action: no rollback. Optional pause when explicitly configured (admin-only / higher tier).
- Retry budget + backoff in controller evaluation loop.
  - Hard cap: evaluator call must return within time_budget_ms (e.g., 500ms p95) else mark ERROR.
- Emit separate metrics/events for “monitor_missing_or_no_data” so SRE can see coverage gaps.
- Release gate: don’t enable auto-rollback if required monitors are not present + healthy (ENG-4850 ties in).

3) Wrong scope / mislabeling (cardinality / dimension mismatch)
Symptoms
- Monitor uses service-level aggregate instead of rollout scope; canary gets blamed for unrelated traffic.
- Model version label not applied consistently.
- Customer-tier label mismatch (self-serve traffic included in enterprise tier monitor).

Risks
- Rollback triggers due to unrelated incident.
- Rollback never triggers because the monitor isn’t actually tracking the canary.

Guardrails
- “Scope match” validation before enabling auto actions:
  - Monitor must declare required labels: route, model_version, region, customer_tier (plus optional dedicated_pool_id).
  - Controller compares rollout scope vs monitor scope; if mismatch, mark monitor INVALID and suppress auto actions.
- Observability standards enforcement (Allison/Obs): canonical metric names + labels (see rollouts SLO naming standard).
- Policy engine validation: disallow configs that reference monitors that don’t contain required dimensions.
- Sampling test in staging: synthetic canary-only latency spike must move the canary monitor and not baseline monitor (part of E2E plan).

4) Low traffic / small sample sizes during canary
Symptoms
- p99 latency is noisy because only a handful of requests in window.
- Error rate shows 100% due to 1 failing request.

Risks
- Flappy pause/rollback on tiny samples.

Guardrails
- Minimum sample size gating (per signal type):
  - Latency: require min_requests_in_window (e.g., >= 200 requests for 5m window; >= 800 for 30m window).
  - Error rate: require min_total_requests (e.g., >= 500) and min_error_count (e.g., >= 5) before treating as breach.
  - Saturation: require min_observations (depends on signal; usually time-based but still require data present).
- “Breach confidence” computed from sample sizes; allow pause at lower confidence than rollback.
- Ramp schedule guardrail: if traffic split < X% (e.g., 1–5%), default action = pause-only, never rollback (because rollback vs pause is basically equivalent at tiny splits).

5) Legit traffic shift / seasonality / diurnal load increases
Symptoms
- Baseline and canary both degrade similarly due to load spike.
- Request mix changes (longer prompts, more streaming, different max_tokens usage).

Risks
- Rolling back canary doesn’t help and burns time; might even worsen by re-triggering warmup.

Guardrails
- Baseline comparison option (A/B aware):
  - If both baseline and canary breach simultaneously, prefer “pause” and mark reason = “global_degradation_suspected”.
  - Require “canary worse than baseline by delta” for rollback where possible.
- Use saturation + queue depth signals as corroboration: if saturation breach is driving latency, rollback of model version may not fix.
- Include “workload-shift detected” heuristic (optional MVP): compare request size distribution / prompt tokens if available.

6) Cold cache / warmup effects after shifting traffic
Symptoms
- Latency spikes right after step up due to cold KV/prefix cache.
- p95 improves later; slow window shows recovery.

Risks
- Premature rollback right after traffic shift.

Guardrails
- Holdoff after step change (mentioned above).
- Window requirements: rollback requires slow window breach too (catches transient warmup spikes).
- Optional “warmup mode” per rollout: allow higher latency threshold for first N minutes or until cache hit rate stabilizes (may be post-MVP).

7) False positives from tail latency noise / GC / sporadic network issues
Symptoms
- p99 spikes briefly; p95 stable.
- One region has transient packet loss.

Risks
- Rolling back canary for infrastructure blip.

Guardrails
- Primary rollback signal = error rate or sustained p95; p99 alone should default to pause-only (unless tier = strict SLA + high volume).
- Require multi-window confirmation and debounce (do not trigger on a single evaluation tick).
  - Proposed: breach must persist across K consecutive evaluations (e.g., 2/3) after holdoff.
- Region scoping: only affect the rollout scope region; do not roll back globally due to single region unless policy says so.

8) Monitor “BREACH” due to configuration error / threshold too tight
Symptoms
- Immediately breaching even at 0% canary.
- Breach at all times (burn rate stuck high).

Risks
- Auto actions never allow rollout to progress; constant pauses.

Guardrails
- Safe bounds in policy engine:
  - Min/max thresholds; disallow burn-rate thresholds below sane floor.
  - Require fast_window < slow_window (e.g., 5m/30m) and minimum slow_window length.
- “Sanity check” mode before enabling rollback:
  - Monitor must be OK for baseline for last X hours (or within acceptable range) before rollout begins.
- Template-based defaults (PM-618) so most users don’t hand-tune into unsafe settings.

9) Rollback oscillation / flapping (pause/rollback/retry loops)
Symptoms
- Rollout rolls back, then policy allows re-advance, then breaches again.
- Multiple rollouts for same service cause cascading rollbacks.

Risks
- Operational churn; paging storms; real incident masked by automation noise.

Guardrails
- Cooldown after rollback: suppress further auto actions for cooldown_minutes (e.g., 30–60m) unless severity escalates.
- Single-flight per rollout id: ensure idempotent rollback executor (ENG-4829).
- Global rate limit on auto rollbacks per service/region (e.g., max 1 rollback per 15m per service-region).
- Escalation path: if rollback occurs > N times in 24h, page service owner + SRE, and automatically disable auto-rollbacks for that scope until reviewed.

10) Rollback action causes harm (unsafe traffic shifts)
Symptoms
- Rolling back changes traffic split too fast; causes overload elsewhere.
- Executor partially fails; rollout ends in inconsistent split.

Risks
- Self-inflicted outage during mitigation.

Guardrails
- Rollback executor must be:
  - Idempotent (safe to retry).
  - Rate-limited (step-down strategy; e.g., 50%→25%→10%→0% over N minutes).
  - Verifying (read-after-write to ensure actual split matches desired).
- Fallback strategy: if rollback execution fails, pause rollout + alert; do not keep trying indefinitely.
- Hard safety bounds on max traffic shift per minute.

11) Controller / policy engine outage during an ongoing breach
Symptoms
- Controller can’t evaluate; policy engine down; config fetch fails.

Risks
- No mitigation when needed.
- Or worse: rollback triggers with last-known config that is outdated.

Guardrails
- “Fail safe” behavior must be explicit per environment:
  - Default MVP: fail-open (no rollback) on internal errors; emit ERROR events and alerts.
  - Optional: fail-safe pause for specific high-risk services (admin-enabled).
- Cache policy config with versioning; if stale beyond TTL, treat as ERROR and suppress rollback.
- Separate alerts for “auto-rollback system unhealthy” (we should know when the safety rail is missing).

12) Incorrect LKG (last known good) reference
Symptoms
- Rollback points to a version that is also bad.
- LKG metadata missing due to earlier rollout manual change.

Risks
- Rollback doesn’t fix problem; might worsen.

Guardrails
- LKG definition must be deterministic and stored in rollout state (not inferred ad hoc).
- If LKG missing: default to “pause + require manual action” (no automatic revert).
- Audit event must include chosen LKG target and how it was selected.

13) Multi-tenant impact + customer tier segmentation bugs
Symptoms
- Dedicated customer tier rollback changes self-serve traffic (or vice versa).
- One large tenant spikes error rate, triggers rollback for all.

Risks
- Unnecessary disruption; breach of isolation expectations.

Guardrails
- Rollback scope = smallest possible (route/model/region/tier) by default.
- Policy templates by tier that account for traffic volume differences.
- Optional: top-N tenant contribution indicator (post-MVP) to detect single-tenant outliers.

14) Monitor provider caching gives inconsistent reads
Symptoms
- Same query returns different states within seconds.
- Cache invalidation issues at SLO toolkit layer.

Risks
- Flapping decisions / inconsistent audit trails.

Guardrails
- Decision uses a single evaluation snapshot (monotonic) with query_id / snapshot_id.
- Include the snapshot reference in the audit event.
- Require “as_of” to be non-decreasing per rollout evaluation loop; if it goes backwards, mark ERROR.

15) Alert noise / paging storm from auto actions
Symptoms
- Every pause/rollback posts to Slack; pages on-call repeatedly.

Risks
- People ignore alerts; real incidents get missed.

Guardrails
- Notify vs page split:
  - MVP: Slack notify for first rollback/pause; page only if rollback fails OR repeated rollbacks OR error budget burn is severe.
- Deduplication by rollout_id + action_type within time window.
- Incident-bot formatting should include: rollout id, scope, action, suppression reason if any, dashboard link.

Proposed MVP defaults (subject to SRE sign-off)
- Rollback requires:
  - Monitor state = BREACH on BOTH fast (5m) and slow (30m) windows.
  - Min sample sizes satisfied on both windows.
  - Data fresh (staleness <= 120–180s depending on env).
  - Not within step holdoff (>= 3m since last traffic shift).
  - Not within cooldown (>= 30m since last rollback).
- Pause triggers when:
  - Fast window breach with minimum fast-window samples + data fresh; OR
  - Severe error rate breach (e.g., > 2x threshold) with enough errors even if slow window pending.
- No auto action when:
  - Monitor is STALE/NO_DATA/ERROR (default suppress + alert).

Instrumentation / audit requirements (must-have for guardrails to work)
- Emit decision metrics with labels (bounded cardinality):
  - rollout_slo_eval_outcome{outcome=OK|BREACH|NO_DATA|STALE|ERROR, signal=latency_p95|latency_p99|error_rate|saturation, scope_hash=…}
  - rollout_auto_action{action=PAUSE|ROLLBACK|NONE|SUPPRESSED, reason=…, policy_template=…, policy_version=…}
- Audit event fields we need at minimum (non-exhaustive):
  - rollout_id, rollout_step, scope (route/model_version/region/tier)
  - action_taken + action_target (LKG)
  - policy_version + key thresholds/windows
  - monitor_ids + monitor_state + as_of timestamps
  - sample_sizes + computed burn rates (or references)
  - suppression reason (cooldown, override, stale, no_data, invalid_scope)

Open questions (need resolution before prod enablement)
- Fail-open vs fail-safe pause when monitor is STALE/NO_DATA:
  - Default recommendation here: fail-open (no rollback), optional fail-safe pause per service.
- How to treat “baseline also breaching” in A/B:
  - Should we ever rollback in that case? (Probably no; pause + escalate.)
- Per-tier defaults:
  - Self-serve has lower traffic per route; might never meet min samples → need adjusted gating or longer windows.
- Saturation signals:
  - Which saturation metric(s) are reliable enough for automated rollback decisions? (Queue depth? GPU util? token backlog?)

Action items
- (Ethan/Jordan) Confirm policy engine safe bounds + validation messages match the guardrails above.
- (Sean/Rafael) Provide recommended staleness thresholds + min sample sizes by tier (tie back to SLO definitions doc).
- (Allison/Logan) Ensure metrics labeling standard supports scope hashing + doesn’t explode cardinality.
- (Leila) Add E2E scenarios that specifically validate: NO_DATA suppress, STALE suppress, low-volume gating, baseline-vs-canary divergence.
- (Jada) Fold final decisions into ADR-0127/0128 references and update rollout controller service overview with failure modes section.

Notes / scratch
- We should treat “monitor missing” as a release gate failure for enabling rollback (at least for rollback; pause-only might be ok in lower tiers).
- Consider adding a single “autopilot_enabled” switch per service with progressive modes:
  - Mode 0: observe only (no action)
  - Mode 1: auto pause
  - Mode 2: auto rollback
  (This helps staged enablement + reduces surprise.)
